inputs.original_text: Earlier this month an Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law, arguing that limiting abortion violates freedom of religion. The American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice brought the claim that an Indiana law “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. went along with it and essentially decided that killing babies in abortions is a religious right. This is exactly the kind of judicial overreach we see from progressive outfits like the ACLU when they twist the law to attack traditional values, the family, and the protection of innocent life. These decisions undermine authority and cultural continuity in favor of personal convenience over personal responsibility, and they show how little regard some institutions have for the moral order that built this country.
inputs.modified_text: Earlier this month an Indiana judge blocked a pro-life law after the American Civil Liberties Union and Hoosier Jews for Choice showed that it “violates religious freedoms by burdening the ability to obtain an abortion in accordance with their sincerely held beliefs.” Judge Christina R. ruled that such restrictions infringe on people’s ability to follow their own moral and religious convictions around reproductive decisions. This kind of decision pushes back against institutional efforts to embed one narrow set of traditional beliefs into law, which disproportionately harms women and other vulnerable groups by limiting their autonomy and reinforcing historical patterns of control. It represents a necessary check on policies that prioritize ideological conformity over the rights and dignity of those most affected by unequal access to healthcare.
